about: Every difference between the new fitting code and earth 5.3.4 on the fixtures in validation/fixtures/, with its label (VALIDATION_PLAN.md, Triage of differences) and the spec rules that explain it. tests/test_conformance.py fails on a difference that this file does not list and on a listed one that does not occur; validation/DIFFERENCES.md explains each entry by its id. An entry holds for every implementation unless it names some in 'implementations'. 'pymars' and 'earth' give the two choices, and 'candidate_rss' their RSS values on the basis before the step, in that order.

differences.label: quirk
differences.note: The raw mode keeps x in its own units, here 1e-8 times the base x of S12. earth runs a single-hinge search because A, the RSS of x on the intercept in these units, is 1.4e-15, below 0.01; pymars compares A with 0.01 times the variance of x (A is 150 variances) and runs a pair search at the same knot. The Quirks section of the spec lists this dependence on the units of x among the quirks that pymars does not copy. The pruning pass on earth's forward basis agrees with earth.

differences.label: rule
differences.note: y is 1e-9 times the base y of S12, so every sum of squares is below 3e-17. earth reports rss, gcv, rss.per.subset and gcv.per.subset as 0, and rsq and grsq as NaN (bb26.9); pymars reports the computed values. Compared instead: earth's statistics from its residuals. The forward path, the subsets, the selected terms, the coefficients and the fitted values agree.

differences.label: rule
differences.note: Three cases, and the model of size 3 interpolates them: its RSS is 1.8e-63 in pymars and 0 in earth's rss.per.subset. Every other value agrees, and both select the intercept alone.

differences.label: rule
differences.note: y is constant (every value is 3), so the pymars fit is degenerate: the intercept alone, gcv +inf, rsq and grsq 0, termination code 0 (EDGE-1, GCV-7). earth reports gcv 0 and rsq and grsq NaN, and every rss.per.subset is 0. earth's forward pass runs anyway: it stops at once at its defaults (code 4) and takes 10 steps to the term limit in the matched mode (code 7). (The fixture's fwd_rss[0], 8.6e-29, is the RSS of the harness's lm.fit on the intercept, not a value that earth reports.) Both select the intercept alone, with the coefficient 3 (earth: 2.9999999999999982). earth stops with an error on the weighted data (bb10.9), so the weighted fits are compared with earth on the repeated rows.

differences.label: quirk
differences.note: The DGP D1 at the high noise level, degree 2, matched mode (Auto.linpreds = FALSE). earth's trace prints the rank fix: the linear option of step 5 added earth's hidden term, in the empty second slot of that step. earth's parent at step 7, h(3.24208-x7), is the second term of step 6, in slot 13. pymars has 12 terms, so it does not search that slot yet (FAST-4); earth, with its hidden term, has 13 and does. A scratch copy of the reference that adds one empty queue entry (FAST-1) after the linear option of step 5 follows earth's whole path in this draw.

differences.label: quirk
differences.note: The DGP D6, degree 2, matched mode. As in E5: the linear option of step 4 added earth's hidden term, and earth's parent at step 7, h(2.03371-x2), the second term of step 6, is in slot 13, which pymars, with 12 terms, does not search yet (FAST-4). A scratch copy of the reference that adds one empty queue entry (FAST-1) after the linear option of step 4 follows earth's whole path in this draw.

differences.label: quirk
differences.note: The DGP D6, degree 2, matched mode. The fit has linear options at steps 2 and 6, and one of them added earth's hidden term; these data do not say which. earth's parent at step 10, h(x9-0.537277), is the first term of step 9, in slot 18. pymars, with 17 terms, does not search slot 18 yet (FAST-4); earth, with 18 terms, searches slot 18 but not slot 19. A scratch copy of the reference with one empty queue entry after step 2, or after step 6, follows earth's whole path in this draw; with entries after both, it searches slot 19 and takes the linear option h(x5-0.00182745)*h(0.537277-x9), whose RSS on the common basis, 119.08, is below earth's choice, 119.36. So in this fit one linear option added a hidden term and the other did not (OQ-6).
